summary: Aermotor fire tower on the Malheur NF, Grant County, Oregon; NHLR-registered 2002; no fire use, recommended for decommissioning in a 2018 draft plan; still listed as standing and unmanned in Cheryl Hill's Oregon list as of July 2026.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab; 16 by 20 foot wood-frame living quarters
facts.status_note: Standing but abandoned for fire use; slated for decommissioning per a 2021 trip report and a 2018 draft Forest plan; still listed as standing in Cheryl Hill's Oregon list as of July 2026

access.note: No closure order found. A 2018 draft plan recommends securing the towers against public access, and a 2021 trip report says the Forest deemed the tower unfit for use.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Malheur National Forest

events.note: Forest Lookouts structural inventory, firelookout.com and a 2021 trip report date the tower to 1929. NHLR and Cheryl Hill's list say 1928.
Lookout-fireman Truxton Dalton reported a smoke on July 12, 1929.
A 64-foot tower replaced the old 90-foot tree lookout, per a May 1930 letter quoted by Forest Lookouts.
A local boy was employed as lookout; the travelers' register logged 180 visitors in the two seasons before May 1930.
Fireman Paul Gillingham was on duty at the lookout in October 1938.
Draft Malheur National Forest facility plan says the tower is no longer needed for the fire program and recommends decommissioning it.
Trip report describes the tower as abandoned but standing; living quarters had broken windows but were in fair condition; structures slated for decommission.
Cheryl Hill's Oregon list, which gives its count as of July 2026, describes the tower as still standing and lists it as unmanned.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Cheryl Hill's list say 1928. Firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts structural inventory and the 2021 trip report say 1929. The story reports both and does not pick one.

Sources give 60 ft (firelookout.com), 64 ft (1930 letter), 67 ft (NHLR) and 80 ft (Forest Lookouts inventory and 2021 trip report). The brief's 18.3 m matches only the 60 ft figure, so height_m is left out of facts.
NHLR gives 6,320 ft (1,926 m), matching the brief. Cheryl Hill's list gives 6,384 ft. Facts omit elevation.
NHLR (2002) says the ground living quarters were on the cabin rental system. The Forest's current cabin rental page lists four former guard stations and Fall Mountain Lookout only, not this site.

notes_for_editor: Build year and height conflict across sources; the story says so. Cheryl Hill's Oregon list (count as of July 2026) is the newest source found and still lists the tower as standing and unmanned; the 2021 trip report is the newest detailed condition report, so today's condition and access are unconfirmed. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on that July 2026 list and the 2018 plan (not in the staffed list). The 2021 trip report says the tower was open to climb although the Forest had deemed it unfit; the story advises against climbing, citing the Forest's unfit-for-use finding. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with 'restricted' based on the Forest's recommendation to secure the towers, not on any closure order. Elevation is a conflict, not an error in the brief.
